A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VideoTemp-o3 work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete Appendices A–G support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v3 reports original benchmark results and component ablations in Section 5, supplemented by ground-truth cropping experiments, training reward analyses, and model-output case studies in the appendices.

after.justification: v4 reports the original benchmark and appendix results and adds inference-time control experiments on VideoMME in Table 6.

M1.justification: The backbone, iterative localize–clip–answer procedure, unified SFT masking, GRPO objective, and penalty-aware IoU reward remain unchanged. Added annotation explanations and inference ablations do not establish a revision to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Training sources, evaluation datasets, tasks, and duration coverage are retained. VideoTemp-Bench's 1,200 samples and four duration groups were already documented in v3 Appendix A. CG-Bench is newly discussed but not evaluated.

E2.justification: New Table 6 evaluates prompt-only re-grounding and inference-time self-correction on Qwen2.5-VL-7B, plus crop-once and no-tool-call variants of VideoTemp-o3. Comparator membership in existing Tables 1–5 is unchanged.

E3.justification: Table 6 introduces controlled inference procedures on VideoMME without subtitles, varying prompting and tool use. Previously reported training budgets, frame limits, resolutions, and generation settings remain unchanged in Appendix B and the configuration table, renumbered from Table 6 to Table 7.

E4.justification: The added inference-control study tests whether prompting, fixed single cropping, or direct answering can match learned adaptive inference. Existing training-component ablations, ground-truth cropping analyses, reward curves, and appendix case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run summaries, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new control table also provides only point estimates.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark and appendix results are unchanged. New Table 6 reports overall VideoMME accuracies of 58.4 for prompt-only re-grounding, 60.5 for self-correction, 63.0 for crop-once, and 62.1 without tool calls. Qwen2.5-VL-7B's 59.9 and the full model's 64.5 are redisplayed unchanged.

T1.justification: The task formulation and Equations 1–6 are unchanged, with no added proofs or formal derivations. The new discussion of masking reliability is a qualitative limitation rather than a revised formal assumption.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same scientific claims concerning unified grounding and QA, adaptive cropping, refinement, training design, data construction, and benchmark performance.

C2.justification: v4 substantially broadens the limitations beyond v3's grounding and task-difficulty discussion. Section 7 adds missed few-frame events, sequential inference overhead, teacher and annotation costs, and the reliability assumption underlying masking. Section 5.4 adds a sparse-skim failure explanation and interprets the new controls; the revised Impact Statement adds source-bias and deployment boundaries.

D1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.2 newly explain handling multiple valid evidence segments, including annotating alternative intervals when possible. Section 5.1 identifies MLVU's test set. These are additional disclosures; the PDFs do not establish changed annotations or a changed split. Appendix hyperparameters and data-construction prompts are retained.

R1.justification: v4 expands discussion of VideoChat-R1.5, VideoThinker, Open-o3 Video, Rewatch-R1, and FrameThinker, adds temporal-grounding references, and distinguishes VideoTemp-Bench from CG-Bench. This refines the existing contribution positioning. The updated VideoExplorer bibliography entry represents the same previously cited work.

P1.justification: v4 locally expands related work and explanatory passages, adds a Limitations section and acknowledgements, rewrites the Impact Statement, and corrects several language errors. The main narrative and appendix organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v4 adds Table 6, adjusts table sizing and placement, clarifies closed-source reference models in Table 1's caption, and reflows surrounding material. The task-breakdown and tool-call figures exchange numbers and positions; their contents and the other existing illustrations are retained.

improvement.justification: Table 6 adds useful evidence for adaptive inference beyond v3's training ablations, while the specific limitations and annotation clarifications improve transparency. The main method and benchmark results remain unchanged. Missing exact prompts and repeated-run uncertainty for the new controls limit the additional experiment's evidential strength, so the overall gain is modest.
